Convert unit-keyed quantities with a member attribute

Source: R/convert.R
convert_scale.Rd

Multiplies (or divides) the numeric value columns of data by the value of attribute resolved for each row's unit – a net calorific value to turn mass into energy, an emission factor to turn energy into CO2, a density to turn volume into mass. Values are resolved along the hierarchy exactly as scale_attributes() does, so a factor stored on a coarser member applies to every atom under it that has no factor of its own.

convert_scale(
  data,
  x,
  attribute,
  from_unit,
  to_unit,
  key = NULL,
  frame = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  na_action = c("error", "keep"),
  collect = NULL
)

Arguments

data

The data, in any supported backend, with a column of codes at frame.

x

A NestedScale carrying attribute.

attribute

Name of the attribute to convert with.

from_unit, to_unit

The physical units of the values before and after, matching the attribute's unit of measure.

key

Name of the code column in data; defaults to frame.

frame

Frame the codes belong to. Inferred when exactly one of the scale's frame names (or its atom level) is a column of data.

values

Value columns to convert; NULL takes every numeric column that is not the key.

source

Restrict the attribute to one source; NULL errors on a conflict between sources.

na_action

What to do with rows whose unit has no value: "error" (default) or "keep" (an NA result).

collect

For lazy inputs: materialise (TRUE) or return the query.

Value

data with the value columns converted, plus two columns named after the attribute: <attribute> (the factor applied) and <attribute>.origin_frame (the frame the factor was taken from), in the input's class.

Details

Direction comes from the attribute's unit of measure, read as "<numerator>/<denominator>": with lhv in "GJ/t", from_unit = "t", to_unit = "GJ" multiplies, and from_unit = "GJ", to_unit = "t" divides. The inverse is allowed only when the attribute's kind is "property"; a "factor" is one-way. No unit-prefix arithmetic is done: a column in kilotonnes must be turned into tonnes before converting with a GJ/t factor.

A unit for which no value resolves is an error by default – a silently dropped row is a wrong total – unless na_action = "keep", which leaves NA in its rows.

Examples

s <- attach_attributes_scale(
  scale_example(),
  data.frame(frame = c("sector", "unit"), unit = c("P", "U5"),
             attribute = "lhv", value = c(20, 30),
             unit_of_measure = "GJ/t"),
  source = "example", kind = "property"
)
mass <- data.frame(unit = c("U1", "U2", "U5"), t = c(100, 200, 50))
energy <- convert_scale(mass, s, attribute = "lhv",
                        from_unit = "t", to_unit = "GJ")
energy
#>   unit    t lhv lhv.origin_frame
#> 1   U1 2000  20           sector
#> 2   U2 4000  20           sector
#> 3   U5 1500  30             unit
# back to tonnes: a property is invertible
convert_scale(energy[c("unit", "t")], s, attribute = "lhv",
              from_unit = "GJ", to_unit = "t")
#>   unit   t lhv lhv.origin_frame
#> 1   U1 100  20           sector
#> 2   U2 200  20           sector
#> 3   U5  50  30             unit
